events.title: Democratisation: closed autocracy to electoral autocracy
events.detail: Derived from a change in the Regimes of the World classification, which is itself built from V-Dem expert ratings. It marks the year a country crossed a threshold, not a specific law or decision.
events.source: derived: Regimes of the World / V-Dem
events.contested: Threshold classifications move in a single step, so the date reflects when a gradual change crossed a line rather than when it began. Read the continuous V-Dem indices alongside this to see the underlying trend.

events.title: Output collapse: GDP per capita fell 27%
events.detail: Real GDP per capita fell from 241 to 177 (constant 2015 US$) in a single year.
events.source: derived: World Bank GDP per capita
events.contested: A one-year collapse of this size usually has several causes at once - war, currency crisis, commodity price, or the end of a political order. This marker says it happened; it does not say why.

events.title: Third Plenum launches reform and opening up
events.detail: The Third Plenum of the 11th Central Committee shifted the Party's stated priority from class struggle to economic construction, opening the way to the household responsibility system in agriculture, special economic zones, and eventual price liberalisation.
events.contested: Whether growth came mainly from agricultural decollectivisation, from township-and-village enterprises, from export processing, or from the simple removal of earlier self-inflicted damage remains actively debated. The sequencing - gradual and experimental rather than big-bang - is itself the subject of a long argument with the post-Soviet transition experience.
events.refs: ["Communiqu\u00e9 of the Third Plenary Session of the 11th Central Committee, December 1978", "Naughton, 'Growing Out of the Plan' (1995)"]

events.title: Accession to the World Trade Organization
events.detail: China joined the WTO, binding tariff reductions and committing to phased opening of services, in exchange for permanent normal trade relations with members.
events.contested: Credited with the export surge of the 2000s, but the counterfactual is unclear since much liberalisation preceded accession. The distributional effects in trading partners - the 'China shock' literature on manufacturing employment - are a separate and unsettled debate.
events.refs: ["WTO, Protocol on the Accession of the People's Republic of China (2001)", "Autor, Dorn & Hanson, 'The China Shock' (Annual Review of Economics, 2016)"]
